- Neither option saves me, but blocking reduces the damage taken.

- Block one **Drake Token** with **Archaeomender** to minimize damage and force the opponent to rebuild.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a keepable 7-card hand that had 4 lands, a turn-3 Pirate flyer (Rishadan Airship), Pirate's Cutlass to auto-attach on turn 4 for a 5/2 flyer, and a powerful finisher in Scholar of the Lost Trove. The hand had a clear curve and game plan despite being land-heavy.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to mulligan down to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. The curve of turn-3 Rishadan Airship into turn-4 Pirate's Cutlass (5/2 flyer) is solid, with Scholar of the Lost Trove as a finisher. Being land-heavy is better than going to 6 and potentially getting worse.

annotations.description: Chose Talrand's Invocation over Teferi, Master of Time. Teferi is significantly stronger here: it can be activated on both players' turns for card filtering, can phase out the opponent's hard-to-block Departed Deckhand, and generates sustained advantage. With Feat of Resistance in hand to protect it and Exclude for future turns, Teferi would have been the better build-around. Talrand's Invocation provides immediate board presence but doesn't answer the Deckhand and offers no ongoing advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Talrand's Invocation to create two 2/2 flying Drakes
annotations.betterLine: Cast Teferi, Master of Time, immediately +1 to draw and discard for card selection, with the option to -3 to phase out Departed Deckhand on the opponent's turn if needed

annotations.description: Cast Siege Striker (a mediocre 1/1 double strike) instead of Teferi, Master of Time when the opponent was almost completely tapped out. Teferi is one of the strongest cards in limited, providing card filtering every turn, the ability to phase out threats, and activating at instant speed. The opponent being tapped out makes this the ideal window to deploy it safely.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Teferi, Master of Time for 2UU while the opponent is tapped out of colored mana. Teferi immediately provides card filtering with +1 and threatens to phase out the Departed Deckhand, generating significant ongoing value.

annotations.description: Cast Chart a Course in the precombat main phase, forcing a discard. Departed Deckhand (can't be blocked except by Spirits) was available to attack, and all opponent creatures were tapped. Attacking first and casting Chart a Course postcombat would have avoided the discard, netting an extra card.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Chart a Course precombat, drawing 2 and discarding 1
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Departed Deckhand first (unblockable with all opponent creatures tapped), then cast Chart a Course postcombat to draw 2 without discarding

annotations.description: Discarded Chromatic Sphere instead of a surplus Island. With 5 lands already in play and 2 Islands in hand, one Island is redundant. Chromatic Sphere provides a cheap cantrip (card draw), potential color fixing, and is an artifact that can be recurred with Buried Ruin. Its utility exceeds that of a 7th land.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Chromatic Sphere to Chart a Course
annotations.betterLine: Discard an Island instead. With 5 lands on board and still holding one Island, mana needs are covered. Chromatic Sphere offers more flexibility as a cantrip and artifact synergy piece.

annotations.description: Departed Deckhand has 'can't be blocked except by Spirits' and Siege Striker is a Human Soldier, not a Spirit, so this block should be illegal. Even if the game engine allows it, Siege Striker (1/1 double strike, dealing 2 total damage) would die to the 3/3 Departed Deckhand without killing it - a terrible trade sacrificing a high-potential creature with double strike and the tap-for-pump ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Departed Deckhand with Siege Striker
annotations.betterLine: Don't block - take 3 damage (going to 13 life) and preserve Siege Striker, which has significant offensive value with double strike and its ability to tap other creatures for +1/+1 counters when attacking.

annotations.description: Chose protection from Black on Siege Striker via Feat of Resistance, but the opponent is playing a mono-blue deck with no black cards visible anywhere. Protection from Blue would have protected Siege Striker from any blue removal spells the opponent might have in their 5-card hand, and would make it unblockable by blue creatures in future combats.
annotations.betterLine: Choose protection from Blue, since the opponent is clearly playing a blue deck and protection from blue would guard against blue removal spells and make Siege Striker unblockable by blue creatures.

annotations.description: Discarding Exclude over Teferi's Ageless Insight in a race situation where the game should end in 1-2 combat steps. Exclude (3 mana counterspell + draw) provides interactive protection against opponent's threats, while Teferi's Ageless Insight (4 mana enchantment) is a 'win more' card that requires setup with Teferi and won't impact the board in a close race at 11 vs 10 life.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Teferi's Ageless Insight instead, keeping Exclude as cheap interaction to counter a potential blocker or threat that could stabilize the opponent, and Secure the Scene as backup removal for Juggernaut.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Teferi's +1 loyalty ability (loot) in response to Archaeomender on the stack. With the opponent at 4 life and lethal on board next turn with two 3/3 flying Drakes, looting now could find interaction to protect against whatever artifact the Archaeomender returns. There's no downside to using the +1 here - it builds loyalty and provides card selection.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Teferi, Master of Time
annotations.betterLine: Activate Teferi's +1 to loot (draw then discard), gaining card selection and building loyalty to 5 before the Archaeomender resolves. This could find answers to whatever the opponent retrieves from their graveyard.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Teferi, Master of Time's +1 loyalty ability (draw then discard) while it was available on the stack. With the opponent at 4 life and all of QwCdr's creatures tapped, the free card filtering could help find a way to close the game (like a burn spell or way to untap). Going from 4 to 5 loyalty is also pure upside. There's no reason to decline this activation.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Teferi's +1 ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Teferi's +1 to draw a card and discard a card, gaining free card selection and building loyalty toward future abilities.

annotations.description: At 4 life facing two 3/3 flying Drake tokens and a 3/3 Siege Striker, MstLg Fate used Aether Spellbomb's draw mode instead of the bounce mode. Bouncing a Drake token would permanently destroy it (tokens cease to exist when returned to hand), removing 3 flying damage from next turn's attack. With only 4 life and no way to block flyers, this is the difference between surviving and dying.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Aether Spellbomb's draw mode ({1}, sacrifice) to draw a card
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb's bounce mode ({U}, sacrifice) targeting one of the 3/3 Drake tokens, permanently removing it since tokens can't exist in hand. This removes 3 flying damage and gives a much better chance of surviving the next attack.

annotations.description: At 4 life facing lethal flyers next turn, MstLg Fate declined to cast Lightning-Core Excavator for just 1 mana. The 0/3 body could block Siege Striker on the ground (preventing potential damage) and its activated ability could potentially deal 3 damage to the opponent (at 11 life) or Teferi. While it doesn't solve the flying problem, it's essentially free to deploy and provides marginal defensive and offensive utility.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Lightning-Core Excavator
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning-Core Excavator for 1 mana to get a 0/3 blocker on board that can block Siege Striker and potentially activate for 3 damage later

annotations.description: Passed on casting Lightning-Core Excavator with 1 untapped Island and no other plays available in postcombat main phase. At 4 life facing lethal flyers, the 0/3 body could at least block Siege Striker on the ground, and the activated ability (deal 3 damage) could be relevant for killing Teferi or reaching lethal if the game continues. There's zero downside to deploying it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with 1 untapped land and a castable 1-mana creature, ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning-Core Excavator for {1} to get a 0/3 blocker on board and access to its 3-damage activated ability in future turns.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Teferi's +1 loyalty ability (draw a card, discard a card) which costs no mana and provides free card selection. With lethal likely on board (two 3/3 flying Drakes vs opponent at 4 life), the +1 could still find protection against potential interaction from the opponent's 4 cards in hand, and there's zero downside to activating it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Teferi, Master of Time's +1 ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Teferi's +1 to draw and discard, gaining free card selection that could find relevant interaction or protection before moving to combat.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Teferi's +1 loyalty ability (draw then discard) while Secure the Scene was on the stack. This is free card filtering with no downside - it would have let QwCdr loot through their deck and potentially discard the uncastable Teferi's Ageless Insight. While likely lethal is on board with two 3/3 flyers against opponent at 4 life, declining pure upside is still a mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Teferi, Master of Time
annotations.betterLine: Activate Teferi's +1 to draw a card and discard a card (likely discarding Teferi's Ageless Insight or another low-value card), gaining free card filtering before moving to combat for the likely lethal attack.
